intro.title: English cannot stop at grammar.
intro.paragraph1: Latin America needs an English education that goes beyond content and develops the ability to understand, interact, and communicate in real situations.
intro.paragraph2: The 2025 EF English Proficiency Index (EF EPI) signals an important concern. Among Latin American participants aged 18–20, the Index reports a 57-point decline from 2015 to 2025, while older age groups improved during that period. This trend requires us to examine not only how much English is taught, but how it is taught.

challenge.metricsNote: EF EPI uses results from adults who took the EF SET online. Its sample is self-selected and is not necessarily representative of all students or the full population. It should be read as a relevant comparative indicator, not as a census of the school system.

gap.title: The problem is not motivation. It is the teaching approach.
gap.paragraph1: In classroom practice, the curriculum may devote time to vocabulary, written exercises, and grammar rules while leaving too little space for students to produce English in guided and meaningful ways. Without frequent opportunities to listen, speak, formulate ideas, and receive feedback, English learning can become passive knowledge rather than communicative ability.
gap.paragraph2: The Inter-American Dialogue has documented regional challenges related to teachers' language proficiency, pedagogical preparation, and the systems that support and monitor classroom practice.

lesson.eyebrow: A Lesson from the Evolution of Language Teaching
lesson.paragraph: Language teaching evolved from the Grammar Translation Method, which focused on translation and rules, to approaches that strengthened exposure and practice. Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) ultimately placed interaction, meaning, and functional language use at the centre of learning.
lesson.quote: The goal is not to choose between grammar and communication. The goal is to teach grammar so students can communicate more effectively.

solution.title: The CLEAR Pathway
solution.description: The CLEAR Pathway is a teacher-training system. It helps teachers and institutions determine what to teach, how to organise each class, and how to protect the time students need to speak.

hero.title: Turn a strong teaching framework into English classes that truly work.
hero.description: The CLEAR Pathway brings together three courses for teachers and educational entrepreneurs who want to teach English with greater clarity, structure, and communicative purpose. Each course develops an essential dimension of an ESL class: grammar through a clear sequence → reading through explicit instruction → authentic communication in the classroom.

guidesSection.title: Two distinct elements

items.title: Theoretical & Methodological Guide
items.description: Explains the evolution of language teaching and the pedagogical foundations that support The CLEAR Pathway.

items.title: Grammar Guide
items.description: Organises grammar structures and resources for teaching them visually, orally, and communicatively.

items.title: Class Structure Guide
items.description: Presents practical sequences and routines for structuring classes and encouraging oral participation.

complementary.title: Make what you need to teach visible.
complementary.description: The Infographic Guide gathers grammar topics in visual formats that are ready to project, explain, or consult in class. It is a complementary resource that supports Grammar through PPP Model in particular.

grammarPpp.title: Grammar through PPP Model
grammarPpp.corePromise: Teach grammar through a sequence that leads from understanding to communicative use.
grammarPpp.summary: This course turns grammar into a communication tool. Through the PPP model — Presentation, Practice, Production — teachers learn how to introduce a structure clearly, guide practice, and create a real opportunity for students to use it while speaking.
grammarPpp.includes: The PPP model; oral production before writing; visual support; gestures; realia; guided repetition; games; flashcards; and respectful correction.
grammarPpp.byTheEnd: Teachers can explain structures clearly, move from understanding to production, and design accessible, communicative oral practice.
grammarPpp.idealFor: Primary English teachers, instructors seeking more communicative classes, and entrepreneurs who need a practical foundation for high-quality English instruction.
grammarPpp.ctaLabel: I Want to Teach Grammar through the PPP Model

readingScience.title: Reading through the Science of Reading
readingScience.corePromise: Develop reading through explicit, structured instruction adapted for ESL learners.
readingScience.summary: This course brings Science of Reading principles into the ESL classroom. It helps teachers organise a progression that connects sounds, letters, decoding, fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension so reading is taught intentionally and accessibly.
readingScience.includes: Phonemic awareness; phonics; decoding; decodable reading; fluency; vocabulary; comprehension; and connections with writing.
readingScience.byTheEnd: Teachers can plan structured reading experiences, adapt support for multilingual learners, and connect reading with oral and written language.
readingScience.idealFor: Primary English teachers, academic coordinators, and institutions that want to strengthen a solid reading foundation within an ESL program.
readingScience.ctaLabel: I Want to Teach Reading through the Science of Reading

clt.title: Communicative Language Teaching
clt.corePromise: Design classes where students use English to interact and express themselves.
clt.summary: This course places communication at the centre of the class. Teachers learn to design themes, tasks, and routines where students use English for a purpose: to converse, describe, interview, solve problems, role-play, and present ideas.
clt.includes: Listening and speaking routines; pair work; information-gap games; interviews; role-plays; presentations; and activities for large classes.
clt.goldenRule: Reserve 18–20 minutes of oral production in every 60-minute class through conversations, interviews, descriptions, role-plays, information-gap games, and short presentations.
clt.largeClassActivities: The course includes large-class activities such as Find Someone Who, Guess Who, Hot Seat, Two Truths and a Lie, Story Chain, and Think-Pair-Share. Their purpose is to let many students speak simultaneously instead of waiting for isolated turns.
clt.idealFor: Teachers who want to increase oral participation, coordinators seeking more dynamic classes, and educational entrepreneurs who want to offer communication-centred ESL experiences.
clt.ctaLabel: I Want to Teach with Communicative Language Teaching

items.question: What is The CLEAR Pathway?
items.answer: The CLEAR Pathway is a teacher-training system created by Ana Cristina Volante. It helps teachers and institutions determine what to teach, how to organise each class, and how to protect the time students need to speak.

items.question: Who are the courses designed for?
items.answer: The courses are designed for primary English teachers, academic coordinators, instructors seeking more communicative classes, and educational entrepreneurs who want a practical foundation for high-quality English instruction.

items.question: How many courses are there, and what do they cover?
items.answer: There are three courses: Grammar through PPP Model, Reading through the Science of Reading, and Communicative Language Teaching. Each develops an essential dimension of an ESL class, from grammar to reading to authentic communication.

items.question: Are there supporting materials besides the courses?
items.answer: Yes. The Theoretical & Methodological Guide, the Grammar Guide, and the Class Structure Guide are supporting pedagogical materials that organise the content and resources underpinning the training.
